Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

roommate — a person who shares your room. Example: My roommate is quiet.
share — to use something with another person. Example: We share the rent.
bed — the furniture you sleep on. Example: My bed is near the window.
desk — a table for writing or studying. Example: I have got a small desk.
wardrobe — a cupboard for clothes. Example: She has got a big wardrobe.
window — the glass opening in a wall. Example: Open the window, please.
space — an empty area. Example: There is not much space here.
rent — the money you pay to live somewhere. Example: The rent is high.
quiet — with little noise. Example: The room is quiet at night.
tidy — neat and in order. Example: Please keep your room tidy.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I have got a ...
• She has got a ...
• We share the rent.
• Have you got a desk?
• My roommate is quiet.

Grammar focus: Have got / has got.
Use have got and has got for possession: I have got a desk. She has got a wardrobe. Question: Have you got a quiet room?

Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
Two students share a flat. Ana has got a bed near the window and a small desk. Tom has got the wardrobe and the bigger space. They share the rent.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: Have you got a desk? B: Yes, I have. A: Is your roommate quiet? B: Yes, she is very quiet and tidy.
